title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes the definition begun on the previous page and then specialises it to Mumford–Deligne graphs.

Setting (previous page). A graph G is a set S of vertices together with a set Ã of half-edges. Ã carries a fixed-point-free involution σ and an 'origin' map Ã → S. A 'generalised morphism' G' → G'' is a map S'⊔Ã' → S''⊔Ã'' that sends S' into S'' and commutes with σ and with the origin map. Equivalently it consists of:
- a map f_S : S' → S'';
- a σ-stable subset B̃' ⊂ Ã' of edges that survive;
- a σ-equivariant map B̃' → Ã'' compatible with origins.
The edges in Ã' \ B̃' are contracted: both ends of such an edge must go to the same vertex. So a generalised morphism is a graph morphism defined on the subgraph G_{B̃'}, with the other edges collapsed. In modern terms this is a contraction followed by a morphism.

This page.
- Composition is evident, giving the 'extended' category of graphs: objects are graphs, arrows are generalised morphisms.
- He notes that the isomorphisms of this category are the ordinary isomorphisms. This is correct: an invertible arrow cannot contract any edge, since contracted edges cannot be restored.
- He then supposes G', G'' are MD-graphs (Mumford–Deligne graphs). An MD-graph is a graph with a genus function g : S → ℕ and a set of legs (marked points) I → S, as in (46). These are exactly the stable dual graphs of stable ν-pointed curves of genus g.
- A 'morphism of generalisation' G' → G'' is a generalised morphism of underlying graphs together with a bijection I' ≅ I'' (47), subject to conditions stated on the next page:
  - S' → S is surjective, B̃' → Ã is bijective, and legs are compatible.
  - Each fibre G'(α) is a connected MD-graph. Its legs are I'_α ⊔ B̃'_α, its vertex genera are restricted, and it satisfies the stability condition 2g_β + card(legs) + card(B̃'_β) ≥ 3.
  - The genus is preserved: Σ_{β∈S'_α} g'_β + h_1(G'(α)) = g_α.
- In modern language this is the category (in fact essentially a poset up to automorphisms) of stable graphs of type (g,ν) with edge-contraction morphisms. It indexes the Deligne–Mumford boundary stratification of \bar M_{g,ν}: G'' is obtained from G' by smoothing the nodes in Ã' \ B̃', so the stratum of G'' generalises (specialises to) that of G'.
- The purpose is to describe the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν', i.e. the incidence and specialisation combinatorics of boundary strata. This is the combinatorial skeleton of the 'Teichmüller tower' programme in the Esquisse.
errors: Notational slip in (46): the target graph is G'' but the data are written S →g ℕ, I → S and S' →g' ℕ, I' → S'. Primes are shifted relative to G', G'' (S, I should be S'', I''). The next page indeed continues with S' → S, i.e. the target is unprimed. Harmless.

On the previous page the extra condition (45) on contracted edges is phrased 'même image dans S'. It should be the image of the origin and extremity of a ∈ Ã'\B̃' under f_S (in S''). Also a minor notation drift; no mathematical error.

ideas.what: Category of graphs whose morphisms are 'generalised morphisms' (contract a σ-stable set of edges, then map the remaining subgraph); isomorphisms coincide with ordinary graph isomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: category of graphs with contraction morphisms (Borisov–Manin / Getzler–Kapranov graph categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kontsevich–Manin (1994), Getzler–Kapranov 'Modular operads' (1998), Borisov–Manin (2008) for systematic categorical treatment

ideas.what: MD-graphs (Mumford–Deligne graphs): graphs with genus labelling S→ℕ and legs I→S satisfying stability, as dual graphs of stable pointed curves
ideas.modern_name: stable graphs / dual graphs of stable curves of type (g,n)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen; stable graph formalism in Kontsevich–Manin, Getzler–Kapranov, Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Mumford–Deligne stratification 'at infinity' of M_{g,ν} but not this formal definition, as far as I know

ideas.what: 'Morphism of generalisation' between MD-graphs: generalised graph morphism plus a bijection of legs, with each fibre a connected stable graph of the right genus. This encodes the specialisation order of boundary strata of \bar M_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: morphisms in the category of stable graphs Γ((g,n)) used to index strata of \bar M_{g,n} and in modular operads
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler–Kapranov 1998; Behrend 1997 (stable graphs for Gromov–Witten); Arbarello–Cornalba

missed.claim: Grothendieck gives an explicit definition of the category of stable (Mumford–Deligne) graphs with contraction ('generalisation') morphisms, including the fibre-wise stability and genus conditions, to encode the boundary stratification of \bar M_{g,ν}. This plausibly predates the Kontsevich–Manin / Getzler–Kapranov formalisation by roughly a decade. It is known in substance (any specialist would recognise it), but the priority is not recorded.
missed.quote: On dit qu'on a un morphisme de généralisation de G' dans G'', si on a donné, en plus du morphisme généralisé G' → G'', une application bijective I' ≅ I''
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only: the modular-operad graph category appears here in Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower context. The content itself is standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, early, fully explicit definition of the category of stable graphs with edge contractions, the combinatorics behind \bar M_{g,n} strata and modular operads, written in Grothendieck's own 'MD-graph' language. It is historically interesting as an anticipation, but mathematically routine and well known in later literature.
transcription_corrections: In (46) the targets of g and g' are both ℕ (blackboard N), not 'N' and 'N''.
G', G'' are underlined in the inserted text (MD-graph structures): 'G̲', G̲''.
The previous page's '[-B̃''-] {+B̃'+}' correction is consistent with the image style; on this page, '[-morphismes-] {+flèches+}' is correct: 'morphismes' is crossed out with 'flèches' written above.
'catégorie [-étendue-] des des graphes': the crossed-out word above 'des' looks like 'étendue'/'élargie'. The repeated 'des' is an artefact of the line break.
